$comment: THE HOMEPAGE IS AN EDITORIAL ENTRANCE, NOT A CATALOGUE OF THE PLATFORM'S CONTENT TYPES. This file holds the copy that decision needs, because a page that needs to say something new says it in data/ rather than in a template. Four doors, not eight; the four are the ones a reader arrives already wanting, and each is a real interest in data/taxonomy.json so the name on the door is the heading of the page it opens and the count is the length of that list.
$why_no_map: Eight tiles each drew the same beige silhouette with different blue dots, and repetition turned the signature into background noise: a reader stopped seeing destinations and started seeing UI components. A per-category crop was tried on paper and does not help — mountains, coast, history and food are all continent-wide, so four crops would be four pictures of Europe again. So a door is TYPE-LED with a photograph slot: orientation is words, desire is the photograph, and the map lives one click away on the page the door opens. Cartography orients, photography persuades, and neither does the other's job.
